Up to 7,500 participants are expected to take part in the Nike After Dark Tour women's half marathon on Sunday starting at 5pm from Rozelle Parklands, travelling around White Bay, Glebe and Pyrmont to finish at Tumbalong Park in Darling Harbour.

Majority of the course is off-road however local road closures and shared walkway/cycleway closures will be in place along parts of the course for the safety of runners.

Motorists should take care exiting driveways, look out for runners and follow directions of Traffic Controllers and Police. 

Changed traffic conditions: 

  • Pyrmont 4.30pm to 9.45pm: Pirrama Rd will be closed between Harris St and Darling Island Rd, and Harris Street between Bowman Street and Johnstons Bay Harbour Walkway will close. Managed access will be permitted for Jones Bay Wharf residents during this time – access via Pirrama Rd and Darling Island Rd roundabout. Bank St westbound lanes from Quarry Master Dr to Bowman St will close from 3pm to 10pm 
  • White Bay 4pm to 8pm: access roads in the White Bay ports precinct will close. 
  • Annandale 4.30pm to 8.30pm: Roads through Tramsheds including Dalgal Way and Ross St will close. 

Shared footpath closures and changes: 

  • Rozelle Parklands: shared footpaths within Rozelle Parklands near Lilyfield Rd will close from 3pm to 7pm. Pedestrians and cyclists will be diverted to use Lilyfield Rd footpaths instead.  
  • Anzac Bridge: Cyclists travelling westbound towards Rozelle on the Anzac Bridge will be managed by traffic control on approach to Victoria Rd while runners pass through the area. Cyclists should be prepared to slow down and dismount between 4.30pm and 6.30pm. 
  • White Bay: shared footpaths along James Craig Rd will close from 5pm to 8.45pm. Cyclists and pedestrians will be diverted via Victoria Rd. 
  • Bicentennial & Blackwattle Bay parklands: shared footpaths along the waterfront from Glebe Point Rd to Bridge Rd will close from 4.30pm to 8.30pm.

Thousands of cyclists will take part in Spring Cycle 10km or 50km events from North Sydney to Pyrmont or Parramatta Park. Road closures will be in place along the first 10km to Pyrmont, from there cyclists will continue on to Parramatta Park sharing roads with motorists and abiding by general road rules.

ROAD CLOSURES - 4AM TO 11:30AM:

  • Cahill Expressway and Sydney Harbour Bridge: from 4am to 10:30am the Cahill Expressway lanes 7 and 8, including Mount St and High St on ramps will be closed. On the Sydney Harbour Bridge deck, lanes 3 and 6 will be closed – two lanes will remain open in both directions under a reduced 40km/h speed limit. From 4am to 11am the Cahill Expressway Circular Quay Overpass will be closed in both directions.
  • North Sydney between 4am and 11am: Miller St from Falcon St to Pacific Hwy, Berry St from Pacific Hwy to Walker St, sections of Arthur St, Carlow St, Blue St and surrounding local roads including the High St bridge on-ramp.
  • Sydney CBD, The Rocks and Millers Point between 4am and 11am: including Hickson Rd southbound from Towns Place to Erskine St, Napoleon St, King St, Sussex St and sections of Argyle St, Dalgety Rd and Upper Fort St.
  • Western Distributor from Pyrmont to the City from 4am to 11.15am: including Pyrmont on-ramp, Fig St on-ramp and King St off-ramp. Citybound motorists from the Anzac Bridge will be diverted via the Bathurst St off-ramp to re-join the Harbour Bridge or access City North via Harbour St or Kent St.
  • Pyrmont and Ultimo between 4am and 11:30am: on sections of Pyrmont St, Pirrama Rd, Pyrmont Bridge Rd, Union St, Murray St and surrounding local roads. Cycleway closure from 4am to 11am on Union St between Edward St and Murray St (eastbound)
  • Parramatta Park: the park will be closed to all vehicles from 6am to 2pm.

Special event clearways will be in effect on roads along sections of the course in North Sydney, Millers Point and Pyrmont between 3am and 11am and in Five Dock, Ultimo, Wareemba and Concord between 5am and 11am.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

With up to 80,000 people expected to attend the NRL & NRLW Grand Final, significant delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct.  

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • PARKING: Car parks are expected to be in high demand, fans are urged to pre-book parking online ahead of time to secure a space. A flat rate $40 parking fee applies. 
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry. If you haven't pre-booked parking don't drive to Olympic Park.
  • Carpool with your group and allow plenty of extra travel time as traffic will be heavy.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct and traffic congestion is expected before and after the match. For road closure details, visit the Sydney Olympic Park Authority interactive map.

NRL Prelim Final: Penrith Panthers v Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday 27 September. Kick-off at 4pm, full time around 5.45pm.

With up to 50,000 footy fans expected to attend, significant delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct.
